name: The Cartography of Ash
description: Shot on salvaged flat-screen equipment over fourteen months in the Gray Zone's Ward 9 district, this debut feature from director Priya Nassereddin-Vukovic follows three families sharing a single water reclamation node during a maintenance blackout. There is no score, no augmented overlay, no neural component — just faces and fluorescent flicker and the specific silence of people rationing. Distributed physically on data chips through the Gray Zone community boards, it was never submitted for licensing.
cultural_impact: The Cartography of Ash became a foundational text for the Gray Zone Realist movement, inspiring a generation of Tier 1 filmmakers to reject neural-feed aspiration in favor of unaugmented documentation.
story_hooks: Director Nassereddin-Vukovic has gone missing; her last known location was a follow-up shoot in a HelixCorp adjacent district.
A corporate archivist has been quietly purchasing every physical copy of the film — the party needs to find out why before the last copies disappear.
One of the film's subjects wants their story removed from circulation and will pay — or threaten — to make that happen.
